title: Hi-Tech Pipes Ltd - 543411 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Hi-Tech Pipes Q2 FY27 revenue rose 70.7% to INR1,466 crore on 32% volume growth to 1.65 lakh tons; EBITDA per ton INR3,429.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 sales volume rose 32% YoY to 1.65 lakh tons and revenue from operations rose 70.7% to INR1,466 crore. EBITDA grew 27.63% to INR56.58 crore, but EBITDA per ton slipped to INR3,429 from INR3,540. H1 FY27 revenue was INR2,879 crore (up 74.47%) on 3.21 lakh tons (up 29%), with EBITDA up 24.12% to INR106 crore. Management reiterated FY27 volume guidance of at least 6.5 lakh tons and a 2 million ton capacity target by FY29, and said net working capital days fell to 33 from 56.

segments.name: Solar tubes and pipes (module mounting structures, solar trackers)
segments.commentary: Management says the company is dealing with all top players in this category and expects solar to be among the fastest-growing segments over the next 3 years. Cited India installing 40-50 GW of solar a year, at 20-22 tons per MW, as a roughly 1 million ton market.

segments.name: Export
segments.commentary: Described as performing very well with encouraging international demand, but no figures were given.

segments.name: Value-added products (VAP)
segments.commentary: VAP share is about 40% today; target is 55% in the next phase of growth. Management expects blended EBITDA per ton of INR4,000-4,500 at that mix.

guidance_outlook: FY27 sales volume of at least 6.5 lakh tons.
FY28 sales volume of 8.5-9 lakh tons; FY29 sales volume of 1.1-1.2 million tons.
Capacity to reach about 1.35 million tons by end FY27, 1.7 million tons in FY28 and 2 million tons in FY29, with about 3 lakh tons added in Q4 FY27.
Expects to maintain volumes and EBITDA per ton of about INR3,500 in H2 FY27, helped by lower war-related logistics costs and post-monsoon demand.
At 65% utilisation, the 2 million ton capacity could generate about INR9,000 crore of revenue.
Working capital target to bring net working capital days below 30 from 33.
capex_capacity: H2 FY27 capex of about INR150-200 crore to complete 3.5 lakh tons of capacity; CWIP is about INR200 crore.
Projects due by Q4 FY27: DFT facility at Sanand Unit II Phase 3, API pipes facility, and Hindupur integrated coated steel facility (ERW and solar pipes).
Indicative capex of around INR150 crore each for FY27 and FY28 was cited in response to a question; FY29 capex not specified.
Plan to add 1 million tons of capacity by FY29 through greenfield and brownfield expansion, funded mainly from internal accruals with term loans as needed.
demand_pricing: Management cites volume growth across all major product categories and end-user industries, with solar and exports contributing more.
Demand from data centres is an emerging opportunity alongside traditional sectors.
H1 was affected by the war, energy prices, ocean freight and monsoon; management expects logistics costs and the monsoon effect to ease in H2.
Management expects a much higher demand projection for H2, especially from solar, which it says is at its peak.

qa_highlights.question: How is demand shaping up across end-user industries, and will H1 momentum continue into H2?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 volume growth was almost 30% despite the war and monsoon. Management expects much higher H2 demand, especially from solar, and says it is geared up to meet it.

qa_highlights.question: Market rumours that APL Apollo is buying shares in Hi-Tech Pipes.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the reports are absolutely not correct and that no such development or talks exist.

qa_highlights.question: Growth opportunity and importance of specialised solar pipes over 2-3 years.
qa_highlights.answer: The company entered solar early and supplies top players in module mounting structures and solar trackers. Management is very confident solar will be one of the highest-growing segments over 3 years, with capacity and the full product range in place.

qa_highlights.question: Volume guidance for FY27, FY28 and FY29, and timing of new capacity.
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 at least 6.5 lakh tons; FY28 8.5-9 lakh tons; FY29 1.1-1.2 million tons. About 3 lakh tons of capacity comes in Q4 FY27, taking capacity to 1.35 million tons, then 1.7 million in FY28 and 2 million in FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA per ton of about INR3,500 be sustained with VAP rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it held about INR3,500 per ton in H1 despite energy, freight and logistics pressure, and expects to maintain volumes and EBITDA per ton in H2 as logistics costs ease.

qa_highlights.question: Capex spend for FY27-FY29 and net debt at end-September.
qa_highlights.answer: H2 FY27 capex is about INR150-200 crore; indicative capex of about INR150 crore each for FY27 and FY28, funded mostly from internal accruals. Net debt was around INR300 crore, all term loans and working capital.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 33-day working capital level sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management treats it as a conscious decision and is aiming to bring net working capital days under 30.

qa_highlights.question: EBITDA per ton as volume reaches 1-1.2 million tons.
qa_highlights.answer: With VAP share rising from 40% to 55%, blended EBITDA per ton could be INR4,000-4,500. Management said FY29 EBITDA per ton above INR4,000 is achievable with no doubt.

risks_watch: Q2 EBITDA per ton fell to INR3,429 from INR3,540 a year earlier, and EBITDA grew more slowly than revenue.
Delivery of 3 lakh tons of capacity in Q4 FY27 is needed to reach 1.35 million tons, and FY28-29 capacity targets depend on further projects.
Volume guidance of 6.5 lakh tons for FY27 needs H2 volume of about 3.3 lakh tons, against 3.21 lakh tons in H1.
Management assumes the war's logistics and freight impact eases in H2; the duration of the war is not defined.
Working capital days target of below 30 and the funding mix of capex between internal accruals and term loans.
Net debt rise from the capex plan; the debt-equity ratio moved to 0.23x from 0.18x.
summary.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking, with firm FY28-29 volume and EBITDA-per-ton targets. Answers on the APL Apollo rumour were blunt, and capex and FY28-29 figures were given loosely. The call had little detail on export numbers and no disclosure of segment revenue.
key_quotes: So for next 3 years, I'm very confident that the solar will be one of the highest growing segments for us.
And we hope to take our VAP share from 40% to 55% in the next phase of growth.
We remain firmly committed to our long-term vision of becoming a 2 million ton capacity company.

adds.what: About 3 lakh tons added in Q4 FY27 (capacity to reach ~1.35 million tons by end FY27)
Capacity to reach 1.7 million tons in FY28 and 2 million tons in FY29 (1 million tons planned by FY29 via greenfield and brownfield)

growth.why: FY27 volume of at least 6.5 lakh tons is held and 1.35 million tons capacity by end FY27 (about 3 lakh tons added in Q4) plus FY28 8.5-9 lakh tons (cut from 10) and FY29 1.1-1.2 million tons (new) are guided, but the brief gives only partial specifics: capex of INR150-200 crore for H2 FY27 and named Q4 FY27 projects, with no order book or contracts cited for the volume targets.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA per ton slipped to INR3,429 from INR3,540 YoY; management guides ~INR3,500 for H2 as logistics ease, and INR4,000-4,500 only at 55% VAP (currently 40%).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: About 3 lakh tons (~22% of capacity) under construction with INR150-200 crore H2 FY27 capex, taking capacity to ~1.35 million tons by end FY27, then 1.7 million tons in FY28 and 2 million in FY29.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 FY27 volume up 29% to 3.21 lakh tons; FY27 guide of at least 6.5 lakh tons needs about 3.3 lakh tons in H2, and FY28 guide is 8.5-9 lakh tons.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is about 65%, but the plan to add 1 million tons by FY29 and indicative capex of ~INR150 crore each for FY27 and FY28 is already guided, so further capex disclosure is expected.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY28 volume guide was cut to 8.5-9 lakh tons from 10 and FY27 is held at at least 6.5 lakh tons, which needs an H2 step-up; no raise was signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: The 3 lakh ton Q4 FY27 capacity addition, the H2 volume step-up to ~3.3 lakh tons, and the logistics-cost easing all depend on conditions not yet proven, with war duration undefined.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Projects due by Q4 FY27 include a DFT facility at Sanand Unit II Phase 3, an API pipes facility and the Hindupur integrated coated steel facility (ERW and solar pipes), but no product launch dates were given.

rows.label: Net working capital days below 30
rows.why: NWC days fell to 33 from 56 and management calls it a conscious decision with a target below 30.

rows.label: Net debt rise from capex plan
rows.why: Net debt is about INR300 crore and D/E rose to 0.23x from 0.18x, with capex of ~INR150 crore each in FY27 and FY28 funded mainly by internal accruals plus term loans.

rows.label: Solar pipes demand ramp
rows.why: Management expects much higher H2 demand led by solar, which it says is at its peak, and India installs 40-50 GW a year at 20-22 tons per MW, a roughly 1 million ton market.

tone.note: Management was confident on H2 volume, solar demand and the 2 million ton capacity path, and blunt in denying the APL Apollo stake rumour; it was looser on capex figures and export numbers. Analysts pressed on the Q2 EBITDA-per-ton dip, the FY28 volume cut and the link between capex and net debt.

quality.why: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 70.7% on 32% volume growth (1.65 lakh tons vs 1.25 lakh tons), with management citing volume growth across all major product categories; the brief names no one-off gain, loss, acquisition or weak base, though the revenue growth far exceeds volume growth and price or pass-through effects are not quantified.
